subject: psychology
title: Conformity & Obedience: Studies and Applications
welcome_lead: Three iconic studies: Asch, Milgram and Zimbardo.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology adventure on Asch, Milgram and Zimbardo's Stanford Prison Experiment.
final_note: You can compare the three landmark studies of social pressure.

concepts.def: 1971 role-play study of guards and prisoners.
Lead researcher of the Stanford Prison study.
Loss of personal identity in a group.
Aspect of context that shapes behaviour.

walkthroughs.body_html: 123 male students judged line lengths with confederates giving wrong answers. 37% mean conformity, 75% conformed at least once. Mostly NSI: 'I knew the right answer but didn't want to look different.'
40 men were ordered to deliver fake shocks up to 450V. 65% went all the way; 100% went to 300V. Obedience came from authority, location and gradual commitment ('foot-in-the-door').
Zimbardo assigned 24 students to be guards or prisoners. Within days guards became cruel and prisoners passive. The study was halted on day 6 of a planned 14. It shows the power of situational roles.
